newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DORTMUND GO TOP BUT NEED LUCK ON THE WAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND GO TOP BUT NEED LUCK ON THE WAY.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund bounced back from two consecutive defeats with a 1-0 victory at struggling St Pauli to go top of the Bundesliga on Thursday.
But the German champions looked far from impressive.

A 69th minute goal from German international midfielder Andy Moeller helped Dortmund secure three points but the injury-hit European Cup semifinalists struggled for long periods to break down the Hamburg team.
Dortmund, who meet Manchester United in the last four of the European Cup next month, lead the Bundesliga on goal difference from Bayern Munich who play hosts to Werder Bremen on Saturday.

The 1995 and 1996 champions needed a victory after suffering two successive defeats for the first time since the 1992-1993 season, including their first defeat at home for more than a year by Borussia Moenchengladbach last weekend.
The champions, who were without six first-choice players, sealed the points after Moeller fired home after taking a pass from Swiss Stephane Chapuisat to round off a counter-attack.
"It was a bit of a nervous victory. We were the team who had the luck," Dortmund coach Ottmar Hitzfeld said. "After two defeats these three points were very important indeed."
Injury-hit VfB Stuttgart missed an opportunity to take the initiative in the tight championship race when they were held to a 1-1 draw at home by 1860 Munich
Stuttgart had a disappointing night, letting in an own goal in the seventh minute and seeing their Brazilian striker Giovane Elber sent off in the second half for a second bookable offence.
Frank Posch headed into his own net before Stuttgart equalised with a 13th minute penalty from Bulgarian international midfielder Krassimir Balakov.
Elber, rumoured to be on his way to Bayern at the end of the season, was very angry about the sending-off.
"What the referee did was terrible," he said. "The second yellow card was rubbish because he couldn't see anything."
Stuttgart are third one point behind the leading pair. But fourth-placed Bayer Leverkusen, a further point behind, have a chance to improve their position when they play hosts to Schalke on Saturday.
